integrations.search_check_text: Check the spelling or clear the search.
integrations.seo_intro: Set the title, description and search visibility for any site address: a catalog, form or service page. The rule overrides only the page settings filled in here. Changes take effect immediately.
integrations.seo_robots_default: As the page decides (usually shown in search)
integrations.seo_robots_index_follow: Show in search and follow links
integrations.seo_robots_index_nofollow: Show in search, do not follow links
integrations.seo_robots_noindex_nofollow: Hide from search and do not follow links
integrations.seo_added: Rule added and already in effect
integrations.seo_off_toast: Rule turned off: the site responds as it did before
integrations.seo_delete_message: The address {path} will use the page or site template settings again.
integrations.seo_check_help: See how this address opens now and where each search setting comes from. You can include parameters: /catalog?page=2.
integrations.seo_no_rules_here: There are no rules for this address.
integrations.seo_empty_text: CMS pages take the title and description from their own settings. A rule is needed when they should be different, or when the address has no page in the CMS.
integrations.seo_path_help: Without the domain, starts with a slash. A parameter is fine: with /catalog?page=2 the rule applies when it is in the address.
integrations.seo_match_prefix: This address and everything inside it
integrations.seo_match_help: “Everything inside” for /blog means /blog, /blog/article and so on, but not /blogger. If several rules match, the most specific one wins.
integrations.seo_title_help: Leave it empty to keep the page title. Ideally no longer than 70 characters.
integrations.seo_desc_help: One or two sentences under the title in the results. Ideally no longer than 160 characters.
integrations.seo_canonical_help: Needed when one page is reachable at several addresses: the search engine will treat this one as the main one. Usually empty.
integrations.seo_og_help: The address of an image: it is shown when the link is shared in a messenger or a social network. The file address can be copied in the media library.
integrations.seo_active_help: A rule that is off stays in the list but does not affect the site.
integrations.rd_intro: If a page has changed its address, the old link keeps working: the visitor and the search engine land on the new one. Changes apply at once, with no separate save.
integrations.rd_err_from_slash: The old address must start with a slash, for example /old-page
integrations.rd_err_from_space: The address must not contain spaces
integrations.rd_err_from_exists: This address already has a redirect: change it in the list
integrations.rd_err_to_format: The new address is a page of the site (starts with /) or a full address with https://
integrations.rd_err_same: The old and the new address are the same
integrations.rd_err_loop: This would make a loop: this address already leads back to the old one
integrations.rd_added: Redirect added and already in effect
integrations.rd_delete_message: The address {from} will stop leading to {to}. Visitors who have it bookmarked will see the error “Page not found”.
integrations.rd_none_lang_text: They appear when the address of a page in this language changes.
integrations.rd_empty_text: They appear when the address of a page changes. One can also be added manually, for example for an old link from an ad.
integrations.rd_from_help: The address that is no longer needed. Starts with a slash.
integrations.rd_from_prefix_note: For pages in another language it starts with a prefix: {prefixes}
integrations.rd_pick_label: or pick a page of the site
integrations.rd_code_help: “Permanent”: the address has changed for good, search engines will move the ranking to the new one. “Temporary”: for the duration of a promotion or maintenance.
integrations.ml_enc_none: No encryption (port 25): only for mail inside a network
integrations.ml_server_changed: The server has changed: enter the password again
integrations.ml_load_failed: Could not load the mail settings
integrations.ml_err_host_format: The server address is a name like smtp.example.com, without http:// or spaces
integrations.ml_err_port: The port is a number from 1 to 65535, for example 587
integrations.ml_err_from_typo: There seems to be a typo in the email address
integrations.ml_err_host_required: Enter the address of the mail server
integrations.ml_err_from_required: Enter the address the emails are sent from
integrations.ml_save_invalid: Not saved: fix the fields marked in red
integrations.ml_saved: Saved: emails now go out with the new settings
integrations.ml_save_failed: Could not save the mail settings
integrations.ml_drop_message: The password will be erased after you press “Save”. If the mail server needs a password, emails will stop going out until you enter a new one.
integrations.ml_test_ok: The email was sent to {to}. Check the inbox (and the “Spam” folder).
integrations.ml_not_configured: Mail is not set up: the site sends no emails.
integrations.ml_source_env: Mail works through the server set by the site developer. You can enter your own server below: it takes priority.
integrations.ml_source_own: Mail works through the server given below.
integrations.ml_last_failed: The last email was not sent ({time}): {error}
integrations.ml_readonly: View only: your role cannot change the site mail. Ask the site administrator.
integrations.ml_intro: The site sends emails through this mail server: about new requests, password reset links and invitations. You can find the details in your mail service or get them from your hosting provider.
integrations.ml_enabled_help: If you turn it off, the site will use the server set up by the developer (if there is one). Otherwise no emails will go out.
integrations.ml_host_help: For example smtp.yandex.ru or smtp.gmail.com. Without “http://”.
integrations.ml_enc_help: If unsure, keep “STARTTLS”: it is the most common option.
integrations.ml_plain_warn: Without encryption the password goes out as plain text: choose SSL or STARTTLS.
integrations.ml_port_help: Leave it empty to use the usual port for the chosen security.
integrations.ml_user_help: Often this is the full email address. If the server does not ask for a login, leave it empty.
integrations.ml_pass_saved_ph: Password saved: enter a new one to replace it
integrations.ml_pass_help: The password is stored encrypted and is never shown, even to you. To keep the current one, leave the field alone.
integrations.ml_pass_clear_note: The password will be deleted after you press “Save”.
integrations.ml_pass_moved_help: You changed the server or the login. The old password will not work with them and will not be sent: enter the password again.
integrations.ml_from_help: The address emails are sent from. The mail server must allow it.
integrations.ml_name_help: The recipient will see it next to the address. If empty, we will use the name of the site.
integrations.ml_test_intro: We will send a real email through the saved settings: this shows whether mail arrives and, if not, why.
integrations.ml_test_save_first: Save the settings first: the test uses the saved ones.
integrations.mcp_on_title: Turn on access for AI assistants?
integrations.mcp_on_message: Staff will be able to give keys to assistants (Claude and others). An assistant acts on behalf of the staff member and gets no more permissions than they have. Edits go to drafts, nothing reaches the site by itself. The texts of pages and records are passed to an external AI service.
integrations.mcp_off_title: Turn off access for AI assistants?
integrations.mcp_off_message: All keys will stop working at once. The keys themselves stay in the list and will work again after you turn access back on.
integrations.mcp_enabled_toast: Access for AI assistants is on
integrations.mcp_disabled_toast: Access for AI assistants is off
integrations.mcp_revoke_message: {owner}’s key will stop working at once. It cannot be restored, but the person can create a new one.
integrations.mcp_ex_code_note: One command in the terminal. Each staff member gets the key from their own profile.
integrations.mcp_ex_desktop_note: The file claude_desktop_config.json (Settings → Developer → Edit Config). Node.js is needed: the mcp-remote adapter connects the app to the site.
integrations.mcp_ex_cursor_note: The file ~/.cursor/mcp.json (for all projects) or .cursor/mcp.json in the project. It is better to keep the key in the environment variable ITK_MCP_TOKEN rather than in the file.
integrations.mcp_ex_vscode_note: The file .vscode/mcp.json in the project (agent mode in GitHub Copilot). VS Code asks for the key once and keeps it in a protected store; it will not be in the file.
integrations.mcp_ex_vscode_input: AI assistant key (My profile → My keys)
integrations.mcp_ex_claudeai_note: Customize → Connectors, add your own connector. The server address is above, authentication is “No authentication”, and in the “Request headers” section add an Authorization header with the value from the block below (the word Bearer and a space are typed manually). Request headers in claude.ai are still in beta and not available to every organization; if the section is missing, connect through Claude Code, Claude Desktop or Cursor. The header cannot be changed after saving: you can only delete the connector and add it again.
integrations.mcp_ex_stdio_note: For when the assistant runs a program next to the site. The key is passed as an environment variable (in the env block), not in the arguments. Replace /path/to/site with the folder of the site.
integrations.mcp_copy_failed: Could not copy: select the text and copy it manually
integrations.mcp_readonly: View only: your role cannot turn on access for AI assistants or revoke keys. Ask the site administrator.
integrations.mcp_intro: Assistants like Claude can read the site and prepare edits, like a staff member with a key. An assistant gets no more permissions than the staff member, and its edits go to drafts and are marked in the history. It cannot delete pages, records or files. It can remove a section only from a draft. It never writes raw HTML or scripts, even with an administrator key. It can take a page off the site only if the key has the “Publish” access.
integrations.mcp_off_note: Off for now: the /mcp address does not respond and keys do not work.
integrations.mcp_warn: Everything the assistant reads on the site goes to the external AI service the staff member uses. The assistant sees requests with customers’ phone numbers only if the staff member has selected the “Requests” access for the key.
integrations.mcp_connect_intro: Each staff member creates a key in their own account: “My profile” → “My keys for AI assistants”. Then they paste it in place of {key}.
integrations.mcp_tools_broken: The assistant will not connect until a tool is fixed in the code of the site. {error}
integrations.mcp_keys_intro: Everyone’s keys are listed here. The key itself is not shown: only the last four characters.
integrations.mcp_empty_text: They will appear when staff create them in their profile.
integrations.sf_robots_intro: What search robots may crawl on the site. The standard text hides the admin panel and service addresses.
integrations.sf_llms_intro: A short description of the site for AI services. By default it is built from the published pages.
integrations.sf_robots_file: The file public/robots.txt lies on the site and the site serves it instead of this text.
integrations.sf_llms_file: The file public/llms.txt lies on the site and the site serves it instead of this text.
integrations.sf_load_failed: Could not load robots.txt and llms.txt
integrations.sf_readonly: View only: your role cannot change robots.txt and llms.txt. Ask the site administrator.
integrations.sf_leave_message: The text of robots.txt or llms.txt is not saved. If you leave, the change will be lost.
